Chittim
kĭt´tĭm
n. (Cyprus and the coasts and isles beyond it; the far west of the biblical world)
Hebrew Kittim, from Kition on Cyprus, and by extension the maritime lands west of it. It is the Old Testament's standing name for whatever lies out past the horizon of the Mediterranean.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Balaam's last oracle reaches to it: “ships shall come from the coast of Chittim, and shall afflict Asshur, and shall afflict Eber, and he also shall perish for ever” (Num 24:24). Tyre's fall is reported to the sailors from there: “from the land of Chittim it is revealed to them” (Isa 23:1), and Zidon is told to flee that way and find no rest (Isa 23:12). Ezekiel puts its timber in Tyre's ships (Eze 27:6). And Jeremiah sends the reader west and east to look for a parallel: “pass over the isles of Chittim, and see; and send unto Kedar, and consider diligently, and see if there be such a thing” (Jer 2:10).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines an isle as a tract of land surrounded by water, and coast as the exterior line, limit, or border of a country, particularly on the sea.

expand to see more

ISLE, n. A tract of land surrounded by water, or a detached portion of land embosomed in the ocean.

COAST, n. The exterior line, limit or border of a country, as in Scripture; more usually, the edge or margin of the land next to the sea.

MARITIME, a. Relating to the sea or ocean; as maritime affairs; bordering on the sea.

Key Scripture

Num 24:24 — "And ships shall come from the coast of Chittim, and shall afflict Asshur, and shall afflict Eber, and he also shall perish for ever."

Isa 23:1 — "The burden of Tyre. Howl, ye ships of Tarshish; for it is laid waste, so that there is no house, no entering in: from the land of Chittim it is revealed to them."

Jer 2:10 — "For pass over the isles of Chittim, and see; and send unto Kedar, and consider diligently, and see if there be such a thing."

Jer 2:11 — "Hath a nation changed their gods, which are yet no gods? but my people have changed their glory for that which doth not profit."

Modern Corruption

Jeremiah sends a survey to the ends of the earth and reports that no heathen nation has ever done what Israel did.

expand to see more

Jeremiah 2:10-11 is one of the most devastating arguments in the prophets, and it is made by comparison with the heathen. Go west to the isles of Chittim, go east to Kedar, look carefully, and see if there be such a thing: has a nation ever changed its gods, which are yet no gods? Pagan peoples keep the deities they inherit even though those deities are nothing. My people have changed their glory for that which doth not profit. Israel is convicted not by a standard the nations met and she failed, but by a loyalty the nations show to lies and she would not show to the truth.

The corruption to name is the low view of apostasy that treats abandoning the faith as an intellectual event with no moral weight. Jeremiah puts it as an exchange — they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water — and calls the heavens to be astonished at it. The comparison with Chittim and Kedar removes every excuse: the constancy Israel lacked was not a rare virtue but the ordinary conduct of the surrounding world. A people who have known the living God and left Him have done something the pagans never thought to do.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Kittim (H3794), Chittim, Cyprus and the western isles; iy (H339), isle, coastland; mur (H4171), to change, exchange.

expand to see more

Hebrew Kittim (H3794) — Chittim; Numbers 24:24, Isaiah 23:1, Jeremiah 2:10, Ezekiel 27:6.

Hebrew iy (H339) — isle, coastland; Jeremiah 2:10, Isaiah 42:4.

Hebrew mur (H4171) — to change, exchange; Jeremiah 2:11, Psalm 106:20.

Hebrew Qedar (H6938) — Kedar, the eastern nomads; Jeremiah 2:10, Psalm 120:5.

Hebrew yaal (H3276) — to profit, benefit; Jeremiah 2:11, Isaiah 44:9.

Usage

"“Ships shall come from the coast of Chittim” — Balaam's last oracle."

"“Pass over the isles of Chittim, and see” — a survey of the whole world."

"“My people have changed their glory for that which doth not profit.”"
